title: JPMorgan says cyberattack on third-party vendors may have exposed some customer data
date_note: Published November 19; date of the vendor attack not stated.
summary: Crypto Briefing reports JPMorgan said a cyberattack hit some of its third-party service providers and may have exposed some customer names and email addresses. The report describes the data as limited marketing data, with no sensitive financial data affected and no disruption to banking services. The vendors were not named. It links the matter to a claim by the n0n gang, which the bank has not confirmed.
plain: JPMorgan says outside companies it uses were hacked, and some customers' names and email addresses may have been exposed.
exec: Vendor-held customer contact data is a phishing risk and shows how third-party suppliers extend a bank's exposure.
action: JPMorgan customers: be wary of unexpected emails that mention your account; the bank says no financial data was involved.
impact: Some customer names and email addresses may be exposed; number not stated.

validation.note: Only Crypto Briefing read; no bank statement or second publisher found.
